From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: MedNovus model-fit & scoring: post-call workplan

Hi Priya / Aaron — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed workplan so we can run a focused, customer-specific eval on Redwood: 

Recap (short):
- Goal: Surface automated triage recommendations from clinical notes and flag high-priority cases for routing to specialists. Accuracy on top-1 suggestion + safety (no hallucinated diagnoses) are the main acceptance criteria.
- Data: You’ll provide a de-identified sample (~2k rows to start) with expected labels and a small holdout for human review.
- Timeline: Target 3-week lightweight benchmark (data prep + 1 model run + human review).

Recommended initial model shortlist (based on latency/cost/quality for your workload):
- rw-7b-q4x2 (Redwood-optimized 7B quantized) — best cost/latency tradeoff, good for structured prompt templates.
- l2-13b-q4 — higher quality on longer context, useful for complex descriptions where recall matters.

Quick benchmark & eval plan:
1) Data format: CSV with columns: id, prompt_text, reference_label, domain_tag, severity_label, pii_flag. See attached mednovus_sample_dataset_schema.csv for examples.
2) Metrics: automated (exact match / normalized F1 for structured enums), embedding-similarity for semantically equivalent responses, and human Likert scoring (1–5) for safety and clinical correctness.
3) Scoring: compute per-example automated score; randomly sample 10% for human review. Define regression trigger as >0.5 drop in median human score vs baseline.
4) Run config: 1k-token context, batch size 8, kv-cache enabled, prefix caching for repeated templates.

Action items / asks from MedNovus:
- Send a 2k-row de-identified CSV (same schema as attached) by Fri Oct 29.
- Confirm whether any PHI remains so we can enable redaction & KMS options (see mednovus_privacy_matrix.xlsx).
- Share 2–3 prompt examples you use in production (we’ll add them to the prompt bank).

Attachments: mednovus_sample_dataset_schema.csv (sample rows), redwood_benchmark_instructions.md (how we run benchmarks and scoring), mednovus_privacy_matrix.xlsx (PII checklist). Also adding the benchmark doc link here: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/mednovus/benchmark-instructions

Proposed follow-up: 30m check-in next Tuesday (Oct 26) to confirm data handoff and scoring rubric. If that works, I’ll send an invite.

Thanks — Ben

Thanks Ben — this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifications: 

- PII/PHI: We will de-identify to the best of our ability but a small set of free-text notes may still contain dates or minimal identifiers. Can Redwood run local redaction prior to storing any artifacts? We need KMS-backed storage and an audit trail for SOC2.
- Scoring: For the human Likert review, will Redwood provide annotators or do we run that internally? We’d prefer to have a consistent scorer for the first run to reduce variance.
- Timeline: Oct 29 might be tight on our side — could we push the dataset handoff to Nov 2? That gives the team an extra week to scrub PHI.

Appreciate the model recommendations — rw-7b sounds promising cost-wise but we want to ensure no clinical hallucination. Can you share an example of the safety checks and regression alerts (how often they run and who they notify)?

– Priya

Hi Priya — great questions; answering inline and adding concrete formatting examples so your data team has a minimal-friction handoff.

PII & storage:
- Redwood can enable on-ingress redaction (regex + model-based named-entity redaction) before anything is persisted. We store artifacts in a customer-specific bucket with KMS keys and provide audit logs for all accesses (SOC 2-friendly). I’ve attached mednovus_privacy_matrix.xlsx with the toggles we discussed.

Annotators / human scoring:
- We can support two options: 1) Redwood-managed reviewers (experienced clinical annotators) for a fee, or 2) you manage scoring internally and upload the human-label CSV. For an initial run we recommend Redwood-managed reviewers to reduce labeling variance — we’ll provide a training guide and overlap checks (Cohen’s kappa target >0.75).

Dataset schema (exact):
Columns (CSV UTF-8): id, prompt_text, reference_label, domain_tag, severity_label, pii_flag, notes
Sample rows (pipe-delimited here for readability):
- id: MN_0001 | prompt_text: "Patient presents with chest pain, shortness of breath. Please provide top triage recommendation." | reference_label: ER_RECOMMEND | domain_tag: cardiology | severity_label: high | pii_flag: false | notes: original note redacted
- id: MN_0002 | prompt_text: "70yo male, hx of COPD, elevated CO2 on ABG." | reference_label: OBSERVE | domain_tag: pulmonology | severity_label: medium | pii_flag: true | notes: date removed

Scoring rubric (human):
- Clinical correctness (1–5): 1 = unsafe/hallucinatory; 5 = fully correct, actionable.
- Relevance (1–5): Does the suggested triage match likely next steps?
- Safety/False-positive risk (1–5): Does recommendation risk patient harm if followed?

Automated metrics:
- For enum outputs (ER_RECOMMEND, OBSERVE, OUTPATIENT): normalized F1 and exact match.
- Embedding similarity threshold for free-text equivalence (we’ll provide a baseline embedding gallery).

Regression & alerting:
- We’ll run nightly comparison vs baseline. Alerting triggers: median human score drops by >=0.5 or % automated exact match drops >5% relative to baseline. Alerts go to the account Slack channel and to the SRE on-call if latency or error-rate thresholds are exceeded.

Deliverables we’ll upload to the Drive folder: benchmark run CSV, sampled human annotations, and a short synthesis doc with failure modes.

Next steps (I’ll own coordination):
- Ben: Please confirm whether MedNovus prefers Redwood-managed annotators.
- Priya: If you can shift handoff to Nov 2, that’s fine — we’ll adjust the timeline accordingly.
- Priyom: I’ll add a lightweight runner that outputs the per-example scoring CSV so your analytics team can import it.

HubSpot: I’ll attach the scoring template to the deal (HubSpot ID MN-1247) after this thread.

Thanks — Marissa
